title: lint: field-group-empty reads only stack.objects, so a group the owning object declares for fields an objectExtensions[] entry adds is reported empty and `os lint --strict` fails
body:
## What happens

`validateSemanticRoles` (`packages/lint/src/validate-semantic-roles.ts`) builds its object list with `recordsOf(stack.objects)` and computes `referencedGroups` from those objects' own `fields`. Fields added by an `objectExtensions[]` entry are never seen. So when the owning object declares a `fieldGroups` entry whose only fields come from an extension, rule (b) reports:

```
field-group-empty: crm_account fieldGroups declares "risk_info" but no field references it — the group never renders
```

This is the shape the spec itself prescribes: `ObjectExtensionSchema` says an extension cannot declare a group — "Add the fields here and declare the groups on the owning object", and each extension field opts in with `group: '<key>'`. At runtime the group renders correctly (the served object and its derived form carry the extension fields under the group), so the finding is false.

Because the finding is a warning and `os lint --strict` fails on warnings with no per-rule waiver, a project that follows the documented extension pattern cannot get `os lint --strict` green.

## Where it was measured

- `@objectstack/lint` 18.6.0 (pinned by a downstream metadata app); the same code is on `main` at a998964d — `validateSemanticRoles` still uses `recordsOf(stack.objects)`.
- Downstream case: an app package owns `crm_account` and declares `fieldGroups: [..., { key: 'risk_info', ... }]`; a module package adds eleven fields through `objectExtensions` with `group: 'risk_info'`. `os lint --strict` exits 1 on the single `field-group-empty` warning; validate, typecheck, build and a runtime test of the served form all pass.

## Expected

Rules (a) and (b) judge the object **as served**: the owning object's fields plus every `objectExtensions[]` field folded in, as other rules in the same package already do through `objectsAsServed(stack)` (`lint-autonumber-formats.ts`, `lint-duplicate-field-labels.ts`, `lint-flow-patterns.ts`). Same class as #31998 (security-role-word skipped extension fields) and #18441.

## Suggested fix

In `validateSemanticRoles`, iterate `objectsAsServed(stack).objects` (or fold extension fields into `fields` before computing `referencedGroups` / checking `group` references), and add a fixture: owning object declares a group, an extension adds the only field in it → no `field-group-empty`; an extension field naming an undeclared group → `field-group-unknown` still fires.
